failurePropagationProof.requirement: Structural uncertainty, operative-state ambiguity, unsupported compiler expressions, and verifier contradictions should each route to their own already-existing safe-failure/review path rather than collapsing into one generic error. One bad claim should not necessarily discard every unrelated valid claim in the same document, but no material unresolved claim may disappear silently.
failurePropagationProof.howThisOrchestratorPreservesPerLayerRout: This orchestrator adds NO new failure-classification logic of its own - it calls each already-fixed module's real function and passes its real output straight through to the next stage, so every existing, already-certified routing path (structural health -> operative state's own STRUCTURAL_HEALTH_UNSAFE handling; amendment ambiguity -> OPERATIVE_STATE_PARTIAL/AMBIGUOUS; unsupported compiler expressions -> enforceSufficiencyConsistency's PARTIAL downgrade; verifier contradictions -> MATERIAL_DISCREPANCY/REVIEW_REQUIRED statuses) reaches semantic-coverage's own reconciliation and safe-failure's own reasonCode taxonomy completely unchanged - this is exactly docs/phase-3f1-6-final-foundation-certification/25-cross-module-failure-propagation.json's own already-certified 3-of-4-chains-compose result, now reachable from a live trigger instead of only from a script.

testedProof.scenario: One document containing BOTH an undiscovered material claim (Section 6.02 Liens, $2,000,000) AND a discovered+compiled+verified trusted claim (Section 6.01 Indebtedness, $10,000,000), analyzed together in the SAME AnalysisRun.
testedProof.result: Both outcomes coexist correctly in the same run: instrument.verifiedCount >= 1 (the trusted claim was genuinely verified) AND a real OPEN_REVIEW ClaimReviewItem count > 0 (the untrusted claim was genuinely flagged) - the untrusted claim's own uncertainty never discarded or masked the trusted claim's own genuine verification, and vice versa.

failurePropagationProof.instrumentLevelFaultIsolation: This orchestrator's own analyzeInstrument function is wrapped, per instrument unit, in a try/catch at the orchestrator level (lib/contract-model/analysis/orchestrator.ts's own instrumentErrors accumulator) - ADDITIONAL to the fault isolation the underlying modules ALREADY provide internally (runDiscoveryPipeline's own per-section try/catch; compilePackageToIR's own per-candidate try/catch). An unexpected exception in one instrument's own analysis (e.g. a malformed package-graph grouping) is caught, recorded, and does not prevent already-computed sibling instruments' own valid results from being returned and persisted. The whole run only fails (AnalysisRun -> FAILED) if EVERY instrument failed, or if the earlier, genuinely fatal document-ingestion step itself failed (no source text -> no meaningful partial analysis is possible).
